title: The French New Wave
objective: After this level you can explain how young French critics turned directors in the late 1950s broke Hollywood's rules with cheap, loose filmmaking.
summary: In the late 1950s, critics from Cahiers du cinéma such as Truffaut and Godard began directing. Low budgets, handheld cameras and visible jump cuts became the New Wave's style.

cards.headline: What happens when the film critics grab the cameras?
cards.body: In the 1950s, a group of young French critics wrote sharp reviews of what was wrong with French films. By the late 1950s, several of them, including François Truffaut and Jean-Luc Godard, were making their own. Their films looked cheap, loose and fast. What rules were they breaking, and why did it work?

cards.headline: From the review page to the director's chair
cards.body: Truffaut and Godard came out of the film magazine Cahiers du cinéma. For eight years there, Truffaut was the harshest critic of French films, which he found stale and conventional. The New Wave pushed back against the well-built plot, the merely craftsmanlike approach and the polished 'tradition of quality'. Then, in 1959, Truffaut's semiautobiographical The 400 Blows won the best direction prize at Cannes. The critic had become the one to beat.

cards.headline: Breathless, on a shoestring
cards.body: Godard's Breathless (1960) was made with low-budget, guerrilla methods. Cinematographer Raoul Coutard shot it handheld. When a scene called for a smooth tracking shot and the production couldn't afford tracks, Coutard sat in a wheelchair and was pushed along. Making do became part of the look.

cards.headline: Cuts you can see
cards.body: Breathless ran long. Instead of removing whole scenes, Godard cut inside them, leaving little jumps in time where the trims were. These jump cuts break continuity and remind you that you're watching a film. The New Wave also proved something to the business: a film could be a commercial and an artistic success at once.

mascot.line: Keep this: the New Wave's rough edges started as budget fixes, then became a style chosen on purpose.

cards.headline: The New Wave: breaking in
learned: Critics from Cahiers du cinéma became directors
The 400 Blows won best direction at Cannes in 1959
Breathless: handheld, low budget, wheelchair dolly
Jump cuts break continuity on purpose

questions.prompt: Before he directed The 400 Blows, Truffaut _____.

options.label: ran the Cannes festival
options.rationale: He won a prize at Cannes; he did not run it.

options.label: shot wartime newsreels
options.rationale: The level describes his years as a critic.

options.label: acted in Hollywood films
options.rationale: He started on the review page, not in front of a camera.

questions.explanation: For eight years Truffaut was a fierce critic at Cahiers du cinéma before The 400 Blows won at Cannes in 1959.

questions.prompt: Why was Raoul Coutard pushed in a wheelchair while shooting Breathless?

options.label: He had injured his leg on set
options.rationale: The level gives a money reason, not an injury.

options.label: Godard wanted a joke scene set in a hospital
options.rationale: The wheelchair held the camera operator, not a character.

options.label: French unions banned camera dollies
options.rationale: No such rule; the production simply lacked money.

options.label: The production couldn't afford tracks for a tracking shot

questions.explanation: Breathless used low-budget methods: with no money for tracks, a wheelchair made the moving shot.

questions.prompt: Porter's Great Train Robbery (Level 8) kept action continuing from shot to shot. What did Breathless's jump cuts do instead?

options.label: Hid every cut so the scene felt unbroken
options.rationale: That is the continuity Porter's film built.

options.label: Broke continuity and drew attention to the filmmaking
Cut between two places to show events at the same time
options.rationale: That is Porter's cross-cutting between operator and bandits.

options.label: Replaced cuts with one long take for the whole film
options.rationale: Godard cut inside his takes, adding cuts.

questions.explanation: Porter's cuts carried the action forward; Godard's jump cuts left visible gaps that remind you you're watching a film.
